description: I'm a passionate solo developer interested in programming, artificial intelligence, and innovative technologies. My skills include software development, AI integration, automation, and problem-solving. Through AstravionXX, I aim to combine AI and creativity to build an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that makes space education fun, engaging, and accessible.
summary:
Outpost Sol is an interactive, browser-based mission-control survival game designed for students aged 7–12. It translates complex aerospace engineering trade-offs into tangible, intuitive decision-making without trivializing the underlying science.

Players manage a lunar or Martian habitat across multi-sol operational cycles, balancing power distribution, radiation shielding, life-support reserves, and food production. Every choice imposes authentic physical constraints: activating high-power electromagnetic deflector shields protects astronauts from space weather events but starves agricultural hydroponics and battery reserves.

Grounding gameplay directly in NASA open science—including real coronal mass ejection telemetry from the Space Weather Database (DONKI), biological exposure metrics from the Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and RadLab dosimetry records, and atmospheric dust data from Mars missions—the tool bridges the gap between passive educational outreach and true mission-planning logic. Outpost Sol proves that deep space survival is defined by continuous, calculated resource trade-offs.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

Outpost Sol puts young learners in the commander's seat of an off-world surface habitat. Operating through Sol cycles, players manage three interdependent core resource pillars:

  • Power (MWh): Energy collected from photovoltaic arrays and stored in fuel-cell reserves.
  • Crew Health & Shielding ($\mu\text{Sv}$ Dosimetry): Accumulated radiation exposure and astronaut biological fatigue.
  • Life Support & Biomass (O₂ / Food): Closed-loop bioregenerative atmospheric scrubbers and hydroponic growth cycles.

During each operational Sol, players encounter acute mission events derived directly from space environment conditions (e.g., solar particle storms, dust storms, microbial filter blockages). Players must allocate limited power and crew time among conflicting priorities:

  • Reinforcing active electromagnetic shielding vs. maintaining greenhouse grow lights.
  • Diverting battery power to thermal heaters during severe dust atmospheric opacity ($Tau$) vs. running science instruments.
  • Evacuating to sub-regolith shelters vs. conducting surface EVA repairs.

An in-game scientific advisor, A.S.T.R.O. Bot, provides contextual guidance, breaking down complex principles into accessible terms (e.g., explaining why microSieverts accumulate or how Martian dust affects solar irradiance) while ensuring every choice maintains an unavoidable trade-off.

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

Traditional space STEM content often falls into two extremes: overly simplified trivia or mathematically dense textbooks. Outpost Sol eliminates this divide by teaching systems engineering logic:

  • Demystifying Deep Space Constraints: Demonstrates why human spaceflight is challenging and how real mission architectures function.
  • Classroom and Home Accessibility: Zero-friction entry—instant execution in any modern browser without accounts, installations, or hardware barriers.
  • Low-Punishment, High-Insight Learning Loop: Mission failures do not end in arbitrary "Game Over" screens; instead, players receive post-mission telemetry debriefs analyzing which subsystems failed and why, fostering iterative problem-solving and scientific inquiry.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, and Architecture

  • Front-End Architecture: Pure HTML5, Modern ECMAScript (ES6+), and Canvas API for dynamic celestial and environmental rendering.
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS providing a mission-control responsive dashboard optimized for desktop, tablets, and interactive whiteboards.
  • Audio Engine: Web Audio API generating procedural telemetry bleeps, alert klaxons, and atmospheric synthesis without external audio bandwidth dependencies.
  • Data Integration Layer: Structured JSON schema mapping historical NASA mission logs and dosimetry studies directly into event probability matrices.

4. Creativity and Considerations

  • No Free Choices: Avoiding conventional educational gamification where an obvious "correct" answer exists. Every action incurs an opportunity cost.
  • Real-Data Visualizer Modal: Each event features a "See Real NASA Science" toggle, displaying the actual research study, instrument reading, or mission photo behind the scenario.
  • Cognitive Load Balancing: Keeping core tracked metrics to three primary gauges prevents cognitive overload for 7–12-year-olds while preserving deep systemic interdependence.
